narrative: The model estimated a 55.5% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt—slightly more likely to fail than pass—and that estimate led to denial of your law school application. The most influential factor was your LSAT score. The next two most influential factors both pushed toward failure: your third-year class standing and your first-year class standing. Your middle-income background and full-time status were not among the top drivers. To move forward, ask admissions for feedback, consider whether additional academic work or a post-baccalaureate program can demonstrate stronger law-school readiness, and retake the LSAT only if practice tests show a meaningful gain. Reapply with a clear explanation of any circumstances behind your class standing and evidence of improvement.
